rounds.text: Creative Newtech Ltd demonstrates exceptional top and bottom-line compounding, with 5-year compounded sales growth at 39% and 5-year compounded profit growth at 45% [E14, E17]. This outstanding fundamental momentum outpaces historical share price growth over the same 5-year period, signaling that financial delivery has historically outpaced market appreciation [E20, E53]. Profitability metrics further validate operational strength, featuring a robust 5-year median return on equity of 21% and a return on capital employed of 14.89% against a sector median benchmark of just 6.52% [E10, E23]. Valuation and intrinsic value models underscore significant mispricing, as a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at Rs 2005 per share, offering a substantial 42.9% margin of safety over the market price [E42, E43]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current share price only prices in a modest 10.3% earnings growth rate, which sits well below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E44]. Rules-based screening reinforces this conviction by awarding the company a high-confidence BUY score of 96 out of 100 alongside positive institutional money flows [E41, E60]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -272 Cr in March 2026 alongside a spike in borrowings to Rs 324 Cr [E31, E36].

Despite top-line expansion, Creative Newtech Ltd carries alarming fundamental risks driven by an absolute collapse in cash generation and a massive surge in debt [E31, E36]. Operating cash flow plummeted to negative ₹ 272 Cr in March 2026, creating a catastrophic cash conversion ratio of -3.89x against reported profit [E30, E31]. Free cash flow mirrored this destruction at negative ₹ 275 Cr, while borrowings spiked more than fourfold from ₹ 72 Cr to ₹ 324 Cr in a single year [E32, E36]. Working capital strains are further confirmed by debtor days stretching out significantly from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E58]. Valuation multiples across P/E, P/B, and EV/EBITDA also command a clear premium over sector benchmarks, leaving little room for error [E6, E7, E11]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical sales growth, high return on equity metrics, and positive institutional money flow [E14, E23, E41].

Conceded: operating cash flow hit negative ₹ 272 Cr in March 2026 and free cash flow dropped to negative ₹ 275 Cr [E31, E32]. However, the bear's claim of an absolute collapse ignores that short-term liquidity remains comfortable with a current ratio of 2.36x [E35], and the business continues to generate high returns with an 18.8% ROCE and a median 5-year ROE of 21% [E12, E23]. While borrowings rose to ₹ 324 Cr [E36], leverage is moderate at 0.89x debt-to-equity [E34], easily supported by compounding sales growth of 39% over 5 years and 49% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E16]. Regarding valuation premiums over sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11], these are entirely justified by superior fundamentals, including an ROA of 7.86% versus the 2.6% sector median and an ROCE of 14.89% against a 6.52% sector benchmark [E8, E10]. Conceded: debtor days stretched to 76.3 days [E58], but quarterly operating margin expanded to 5% in June 2026 [E27], demonstrating pricing power that accompanies its robust sales velocity. Finally, institutional money flow reads positive with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their stakes [E39, E40, E41], proving that sophisticated market participants recognize the underlying strength behind the headline cash flow fluctuation.

Conceded: the current ratio sits at a comfortable 2.36x [E35], and ROCE reaches 18.8% alongside a 21% median 5-year ROE [E12, E23]. However, the bull's dismissal of the negative ₹ 272 Cr operating cash flow and ₹ 275 Cr free cash flow [E31, E32] as a mere fluctuation ignores that borrowings nearly quadrupled to ₹ 324 Cr in March 2026 from ₹ 72 Cr a year prior [E36] to finance this cash drain, elevating debt-to-equity to 0.89x [E34]. Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional stakes increased slightly [E39, E40], but this accumulation happened alongside promoters quietly reducing their holdings by 6.86% over the last three years [E59]. Furthermore, pointing to superior returns to justify a P/E of 22.57x, P/B of 4.57x, and EV/EBITDA of 17.7x against sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11] misses the reality that stretched debtor days—rising from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E58]—directly explain why rapid top-line expansion [E14, E16] fails to translate into actual cash collection. Conceded: quarterly operating margin expanded to 5% in June 2026 [E27], but short-term momentum does not erase an annualised volatility of 52.7% [E51] and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% [E50] that expose investors to severe downside risk.

Conceded: borrowings rose to ₹ 324 Cr in March 2026 and debtor days lengthened to 76.3 days [E36, E58]. However, the business maintains a comfortable current ratio of 2.36x [E35], and the broader institutional money flow is positive with foreign and domestic holdings both edging upward [E39, E40, E41]. Conceded: promoters trimmed stakes over three years [E59], yet the long-term fundamental compounding—such as 45% 5-year profit growth outpacing the 37% 5-year share price growth—signals that fundamentals have outpaced the stock and left room for value appreciation [E17, E20, E53]. Furthermore, the valuation multiples that the bear criticises are entirely justified by superior operational metrics, including an 18.8% ROCE and a 7.86% ROA that vastly outperform the respective sector benchmarks of 6.52% and 2.6% [E8, E10, E12]. Finally, historical volatility and drawdowns [E50, E51] are eclipsed by a rules-based screen scoring 96 out of 100 with high confidence alongside robust quarterly operating margin expansion to 5% in June 2026 [E27, E60].

Conceded: the current ratio is 2.36x [E35]. However, this liquidity metric masks a severe deterioration in cash generation, as the company reported a negative operating cash flow of Rs -272 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -275 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. While the bull highlights institutional inflows [E39, E40, E41], these minor increases are overshadowed by the broader trend of promoter selling, which has seen holdings decrease by 6.86% over the last three years [E59]. The bull claims fundamentals justify the valuation, yet the company’s cash conversion ratio of -3.89x indicates that reported profits are not being translated into actual cash [E30, E33]. Furthermore, the bull ignores that debtor days have ballooned to 76.3 days, signaling potential collection issues that contradict the narrative of operational superiority [E58]. Finally, while the bull points to a high rules-based score [E60], it fails to address that the stock’s 52.7% annualised volatility and historical -51.3% drawdown suggest that this "high confidence" comes with extreme risk to capital [E50, E51].
